PJM Governance and Stakeholder Process Reforms
Submitted by

Date
August 3, 2026
GOVERNANCE MUST PRODUCE
ACCOUNTABILITY.
ASSUMPTIONS MUST BE VERIFIED BEFORE
COSTS ARE IMPOSED.
Infrastructure Assumption Verification(TM) | Decision Assurance(TM)

PERSISTENCE ANALYTICS GROUP LLC
FERC Docket No. AD26-7-000 | PUBLIC
Post-Conference Comments on PJM Governance and Stakeholder Reform
Page 2
COVER LETTER
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
888 First Street, NE
Washington, DC 20426
Re: Docket No. AD26-7-000 - PJM Governance and Stakeholder Process Reforms
Commissioners:
Persistence Analytics Group LLC respectfully submits these post-conference comments in response to the
Commission's invitation for bold, actionable reforms to PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. governance and stakeholder
processes.
The Commission should not accept governance reform that merely rearranges representation, modifies voting
mechanics, or creates another layer of consultation. PJM is confronting decisions with system-wide financial and
reliability consequences. Its governance must therefore establish clear responsibility for the evidence underlying
those decisions, the assumptions embedded in them, and the costs imposed when those assumptions fail.
THE OPERATING RULE IS SIMPLE:
NO MATERIAL PLANNING ASSUMPTION WITHOUT A NAMED OWNER, A
DOCUMENTED EVIDENTIARY BASIS, AND A PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY
PATH.
This standard is especially urgent as PJM evaluates unprecedented large-load growth, transmission needs,
capacity procurement, interconnection readiness, and cost allocation. Announced demand is not the same as
executable demand. Executable demand is not the same as durable demand. Governance that does not force
those distinctions into the decision record is not governance adequate to the risk.
The attached comments propose a direct accountability architecture: verified load classifications, assumption
ownership, decision-grade disclosure, independent challenge rights, full electrical cost-causation review, formal
escalation, and measurable implementation deadlines.
Respectfully submitted,
Neil P. Osnato
Founder
Persistence Analytics Group LLC

PERSISTENCE ANALYTICS GROUP LLC
FERC Docket No. AD26-7-000 | PUBLIC
Post-Conference Comments on PJM Governance and Stakeholder Reform
Page 3
POST-CONFERENCE COMMENTS
I. THE COMMISSION SHOULD DEFINE THE OUTCOME BEFORE REFORMING THE
PROCESS
The purpose of PJM governance is not stakeholder participation for its own sake. The purpose is to produce
timely, evidence-based, reviewable decisions that preserve reliability, assign costs fairly, and withstand scrutiny
after capital is committed.
Any reform package should be judged against one question: Does it make a responsible party answerable for
the assumptions that drive a material PJM decision? If the answer is no, the reform is procedural, not
operational.
II. PJM MUST CREATE A FORMAL ASSUMPTION-ACCOUNTABILITY RECORD
For each material planning, market, procurement, or cost-allocation decision, PJM should publish a concise
assumption-accountability record identifying:
• The decision owner: the PJM officer or committee accountable for the final recommendation.
• The critical assumptions: load, timing, persistence, interconnection readiness, financing, operating profile,
flexibility, retirement, supply, and cost-allocation assumptions.
• The evidence: what was submitted, by whom, when it was validated, and what remains unverified.
• The consequence range: the reliability, capital, market, and customer-cost outcomes if the assumptions are
wrong.
• The dissent and escalation path: how a material evidentiary challenge is preserved and elevated before
implementation.
III. LARGE-LOAD FORECASTS REQUIRE DECISION-GRADE CLASSIFICATION
PJM should stop treating projected load as a single category. At minimum, large-load additions should be
separated into the following stages:
Classification
Required meaning
Announced
Publicly stated or submitted, but not yet supported by enforceable commercial, site,
equipment, power-delivery, and schedule evidence.
Committed
Supported by defined financial obligations, deposits, contracts, or equivalent
commitments.
Electrically executable
Interconnection path, upstream reinforcement, equipment, permitting, and
energization dependencies are sufficiently established.
Operationally durable
The expected operating profile, persistence, ramp behavior, curtailment capability,
and withdrawal risk have been evaluated.
PJM should disclose which classification supports each planning decision and prohibit a lower-confidence
classification from being presented as if it were a higher-confidence one.

PERSISTENCE ANALYTICS GROUP LLC
FERC Docket No. AD26-7-000 | PUBLIC
Post-Conference Comments on PJM Governance and Stakeholder Reform
Page 4
IV. COST CAUSATION MUST FOLLOW THE FULL ELECTRICAL CONSEQUENCE
Direct customer funding of interconnection facilities can be appropriate, but governance fails if review ends at the
point of interconnection. A 1 GW to 3 GW customer can alter flows, contingencies, substation configuration, local
reliability needs, and future expansion options across the broader network.
PJM must therefore distinguish, on the record:
• facilities uniquely required by the customer;
• upstream reinforcements materially caused by the customer;
• upgrades that produce measurable regional benefits; and
• baseline needs that would exist without the customer.
A shallow cost-causation methodology can socialize upstream costs even when the customer directly funds
facilities near the site. Governance reform must prevent that outcome.
V. MATERIAL EVIDENTIARY CHALLENGES NEED INDEPENDENT ESCALATION
A stakeholder process cannot police itself when voting power, commercial interests, and institutional incentives
are embedded in the same decision. PJM should establish a formal independent review channel for disputes
involving:
• load forecast durability or readiness;
• material cost-causation disputes;
• use of confidential evidence that cannot be meaningfully tested;
• assumption changes introduced after stakeholder review; and
• decisions where the downside risk is transferred to customers who did not create it.
The review channel should have authority to require a written response, preserve minority evidence, and refer
unresolved matters to the PJM Board or the Commission on a defined timetable.
VI. THE SEPTEMBER DISPUTE-RESOLUTION PROCESS MUST END WITH
DELIVERABLES
The Commission's facilitated process should not conclude with generalized principles. It should produce a public
implementation matrix containing:
• Action: the exact reform to be implemented.
• Owner: the accountable PJM body or officer.
• Deadline: a fixed date, not an open-ended commitment.
• Evidence of completion: tariff filing, manual revision, reporting protocol, or governance document.
• Commission checkpoint: the date on which progress will be reviewed publicly.
PJM DOES NOT NEED MORE PROCESS WITHOUT CONSEQUENCE.
IT NEEDS GOVERNANCE THAT CAN IDENTIFY THE ASSUMPTION, NAME
THE OWNER, TEST THE EVIDENCE, TRACE THE COST, AND CORRECT
THE DECISION.

PERSISTENCE ANALYTICS GROUP LLC
FERC Docket No. AD26-7-000 | PUBLIC
Post-Conference Comments on PJM Governance and Stakeholder Reform
Page 5
VII. CONCLUSION
The Commission should require PJM to convert governance reform into a durable accountability system.
Representation matters. Voting matters. But neither is sufficient unless the resulting decisions are anchored to
verified evidence, assigned ownership, transparent cost causation, and enforceable implementation.
Persistence Analytics Group LLC respectfully requests that the Commission incorporate these accountability
requirements into the next phase of Docket No. AD26-7-000.
Respectfully submitted,
Neil P. Osnato
Founder
Persistence Analytics Group LLC
